overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide minutes within 10 days and by not creating minutes for quasi-judicial meetings, since it is a municipal body without the quasi-judicial exception; it credited the Commission on 31 months and cancelled meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to make requested open-session meeting minutes available within 10 days of the request.
allegations.key_passage: it violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to make the minutes of at least four meetings available to him within that same time period.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to create minutes for two noticed meetings, May 19, 2011 and November 13, 2012, with no evidence of cancellation.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Commission posted notice for these two meetings and has not provided evidence showing that the meetings were cancelled, we presume they occurred, and therefore the Commission should have created and retained minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged minutes were missing for 31 months between July 2010 and October 2014; the Commission said it did not meet monthly then.
allegations.key_passage: In the absence of evidence to the contrary, we credit the Commission's version of events and find no violation

allegations.summary: Three noticed meetings were cancelled and never held, so no minutes were produced for them.
allegations.key_passage: For three of the dates, although notice had been posted, the meeting was cancelled and never took place, therefore no minutes were produced.

allegations.summary: The Commission claimed its quasi-judicial meetings were exempt from the Open Meeting Law, so no notice, minutes, or public access were provided for at least 16 such meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We understand the Commission's concerns; however, we find that the Commission is a municipal—not state—public body, and cannot avail itself of the Open Meeting Law's quasi-judicial exception.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
Create, to the best of its ability, minutes for the Commission meetings held on May 19, 2011 and November 13, 2012, within thirty (30) days of receipt of the order.
Provide the complainant with the four sets of meeting minutes it provided the AG's office, within ten (10) days of receipt of the letter.
Create, to the best of its ability, minutes for the 16 quasi-judicial meetings held between July 2010 and the present.
Make copies of the minutes of the 16 quasi-judicial meetings available to the complainant, and provide copies to the AG's office, within thirty (30) days of receipt of the order.
remedy_passage: Provide Mr. Kaplan with the four sets of meeting minutes it provided our office on June 19, 2015.
